text:
maria: nightly-bot flagged a weird spike in the synth-recall-v2 eval for rwd-3b-q6 on the int6 quant sweep. entity stitching / name fragments up ~8x :eyes:
nightly-bot: automated: run=nightly-2026-03-20, model=rwd-3b-q6, suite=synth-recall-v2, metric=entity_fragmentation_rate, baseline=0.6%, current=4.9%
ben: ugh. I saw a couple samples where 'Alice' + 'Alison' got merged into 'Alisonce' — looks like token merge artifacts. any raw examples?
jia: pasted 3 failing samples to gist: https://gist.github.com/jia/fragment-samples — sample 2 shows partial overlap and then a synthetic concatenation, not just mislabel.
maria: thanks. reproducer command I ran locally:
```
./run_eval --model rwd-3b-q6 --quant int6 --suite synth-recall-v2 --seed 42 --save-fails /tmp/fails.json
```
deepak: quick hypothesis: detokenizer join rule + quantized kernel rounding causing subword boundary insertions. also possible fast-kv cache evict misalignment for overlapping contexts.
ben: can we reproduce on CPU FP32 and q8fallback? if FP32 is clean then it's quant-specific.
maria: FP32 run (same seed) shows fragmentation_rate=0.7%, basically baseline. q8fallback run shows 0.9%. int6 is the only one with big regression.
jia: attaching failing snippet from /tmp/fails.json:
```
input: "Customer names: Alice, Alison, Alistair. Merge them appropriately."
model_out: "Customer names: Alisonce, Alistair."
```
maria: note the generation has inserted 'ce' suffix on merged token — looks like subword concat.
ben: can we dump token ids for that output and compare across quant vs fp32?
deepak: yes running token dump now, will post. this smells like vocab index remap during quantized embedding matmul or fused softmax kernel mis-indexing.
nightly-bot: job=triage-2067890123 assigned_to=eng-ml oncall
maria: token ids (int6): [102, 345, 6789, 230, 99, 12] ; token ids (fp32): [102, 345, 6789, 230, 990, 12]
ben: ah that 99 vs 990 looks like truncation / low-bit aliasing. int6 packing probably clamping high bits.
jia: are we using the new quant table from qtable-v3? I know we changed rounding strategy last week.
deepak: yes qtable-v3 used stochastic rounding tweak. could be the culprit. I'll run variant with old qtable-v2.
maria: repro matrix: q6+qtable-v3 -> frag=4.9%, q6+v2 -> frag=0.8%; q8+v3 -> 0.9%
ben: that pins it to qtable-v3. what changed exactly? deepak?
deepak: we adjusted scale clipping to reduce dynamic range blowup for rare tokens. it improved perplexity but apparently introduced aliasing for some indices in the int6 packer. The packer shrinks scaled values into 6 bits and then we do fast bitpack with SSE kernels. I suspect a rounding floor bug for values near bin boundaries.
maria: mitigation options: 1) rollback qtable-v3 for int6 only, 2) disable int6 in hosted until fix, 3) patch packer to avoid floor rounding at boundary.
ben: for prod, roll back int6+v3 asap. can we hotfix a config toggle?
jam: (infra-bot) feature-flag created: quant.q6.use_qtable_v3 = false for hosted-region-eu and hosted-region-us. will propagate in 5m.
jia: long-term we need unit tests that compare token-id distributions between quant variants and fp32 on a set of name-heavy prompts. add to nightly smoke.
deepak: agreed. I'll prepare a PR that reverts the qtable change for int6 and adds a quant-packer unit test. also adding deterministic rounding option behind flag.
maria: action items: ben to coordinate hosted rollback, deepak PR for packer + tests, jia add prompt set to nightly-smoke, maria to run a full sweep and post updated eval once rollback is live.
ben: on it, ping me when infra flag is live.
infra-bot: quant.q6.use_qtable_v3 set=false in hosted-us, hosted-eu (propagated).
maria: quick follow-up: after rollback, nightly re-run (manual) shows fragmentation_rate=0.72% on same suite. looks fixed.
jia: adding follow-up ticket ENG-ML-1427: "int6 qtable-v3 causes entity fragmentation" with linked PRs and logs.
maria: closing triage thread for now, will re-open if reappears. :white_check_mark:
